text:
Marco: Heads-up 60s review: I wired a small flow where the incident threshold slider sits inline with the notify preview. Goal: you can tweak threshold and immediately see which channels would fire. Prototype: https://figma.com/file/threshold-inline

Anya: Nice. Visuals look clean but two concerns: 1) the slider label overlaps long channel names at narrow breakpoints, 2) when slider value changes the preview flashes and focus sometimes jumps.

Tess: UX thought: show a compact channel list to the right of the slider that updates on drag, but don't re-render the whole preview each frame. Throttle updates to 150ms so SR users don't get noisy announcements.

Priya: Accessibility: if the slider controls which channels notify, SR needs to announce the result after user stops adjusting. Use `aria-live="polite"` and only announce final state. While dragging, announce the numeric threshold but not the channel list.

Marco: Good call. Also, when a channel is excluded due to a suppression rule, I made it get a strikethrough style. Is that readable enough?

Anya: Strikethrough alone is subtle. Add an explicit state chip: "Suppressed by schedule" with `aria-label` for SR. Visual strikethrough + chip covers sighted and non-sighted users.

Tess: For narrow screens the slider moves above the preview and becomes full-width. DOM reorder there currently uses CSS order which breaks tab order. We should keep DOM order static and change layout with grid placements so keyboard remains predictable.

Priya: Another nit: translations can make channel strings very long. On mobile the slider label and channel name collide. Suggest truncating channel labels with `…` and exposing full text via `aria-describedby` and a tooltip on hover/focus. SR should read full label, then the channel status.

Marco: Performance question: when evaluating which channels would notify at a threshold change we run routing rules which are async. Should we optimistic-update the UI to show a spinner on affected rows?

Tess: Yes, show subtle skeleton rows for channels pending evaluation. But don't change focus while pending. Once resolved, announce only if the user initiated the action (not for background polling). Batch announcements when multiple channels change state.

Priya: Keyboard interactions: slider keyboard adjustments (arrow keys/page keys) should move focus stays on slider. After user presses Enter, shift focus to the preview and highlight the first channel that changed as a result. Escape returns focus to the slider. This gives a predictable review loop.

a11y-bot: Accessibility checklist: Slider has visible focus ring, aria-valuemin/max/now, live region for final result, avoid DOM reorders that break tab flow, truncated labels exposed to SR via aria-describedby, suppressed channels use explicit state text, batch live announcements, ensure contrast for status chips >= 4.5:1. Run automated axe + keyboard-only QA.

Marco: Great checklist. I'll update the spec: throttle update frequency, show skeletons, add explicit suppression chips, and keep DOM order stable. Will post updated mock and interaction notes soon.

Anya: I'll check the responsive layout and translations. Also confirm copy: we call it "Suppressed" not "Muted" in product copy.

Tess: I'll prototype the keyboard flow with focus highlights and skeleton states.

Priya: I'll add acceptance criteria to the ticket and plan an NVDA pass.

Marco: Thanks all :rocket: — will follow up with PR for the slider behaviour and a small accessibility test plan.
